# Fairpractice Behavioral Health (`fairpractice-behavioral-health`)

Checks behavioral health billing: psychotherapy codes against session minutes, add-on codes without their base code, crisis time and 90840 units, sessions over a payer's yearly limit, and codes billed under a license type that cannot bill them. Client names are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairpractice Behavioral Health never submits or changes claims. Fairpractice Behavioral Health never reads or summarizes session notes.**

Fairpractice ver 1 · Specialty billing · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairpractice-core`](../fairpractice-core)

```bash
npx -y fairpractice-behavioral-health demo
npx -y fairpractice-behavioral-health mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up counseling practice, made-up clients and clinicians. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`sessions-2026.csv`](fixtures/sessions-2026.csv). Planted:
  - B1: 90837 on November 3 for 45 minutes (the time supports 90834).
  - B2: add-on 90833 on November 4 with no E/M visit that day (October 8 has one and is fine).
  - B3: 90792 billed under an LPC license (the default rules keep it for prescribers). Interactive complexity 90785 with 90834 is fine.
  - B4: crisis care for 100 minutes with 2 units of 90840 (the time supports 1).
  - B5: a fifth 2026 session with Cedar Mutual, which allows 4 a year in the settings.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): example code rates and a yearly limit of 4 for Cedar Mutual. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `bh_check` | List license problems, add-ons without a base code, time code mismatches, crisis time problems and sessions over yearly limits. | runs |
| `bh_write_report` | Write bh-behavioral-health.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and bh-behavioral-health.html into out_dir (default fairpractice-out/bh). | runs |
| `bh_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `bh_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `bh_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `bh_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Fairpractice Behavioral Health never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `note_read` | Fairpractice Behavioral Health never reads or summarizes session notes. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `bh_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `sessions` (required) | Session or claim lines under --root: client, date, code, units, minutes (or start and end), provider, license type, payer, allowed amount |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: rates, yearly_limits, license_rules |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairpractice-behavioral-health inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Sessions (`sessions`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `patient_id` | text (masked) | Patient ID, Patient #, Patient Number, MRN, Medical Record Number, Chart #, Chart Number, Account # |
| `patient_name` | text (masked) | Patient, Patient Name, Name, Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Beneficiary |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `cpt` (required) | text | CPT, Code, Procedure, Procedure Code, CPT/HCPCS, HCPCS, Service Code, Proc Code |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `start` | text | Start, Start Time, Time In |
| `end` | text | End, End Time, Time Out |
| `provider` | text (masked) | Provider, Rendering Provider, Rendering, Clinician, Therapist, Physician, Doctor, Practitioner |
| `license` | text | License, License Type, Credential, Credentials, Provider Type, Degree |
| `payer` | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Insurance, Insurance Name, Plan, Plan Name, Payor |
| `allowed` | amount | Allowed, Allowed Amount, Expected, Expected Payment, Fee Schedule |

## Settings file (`bh_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `rates` | Expected payment by code, for dollar estimates |
| `yearly_limits` | Sessions a year each payer allows per patient, by payer name |
| `license_rules` | Licenses allowed to bill a code; a trailing * covers a code range. Replaces the default rules (prescriber codes and psychological testing). |

## Memory

`bh_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `bh_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairpractice-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairpractice-behavioral-health": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairpractice-behavioral-health",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairpractice-behavioral-health -- npx -y fairpractice-behavioral-health mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairpractice-behavioral-health tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairpractice-behavioral-health sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairpractice-behavioral-health inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairpractice-behavioral-health call bh_check '{"sessions":"<sessions>"}'
fairpractice-behavioral-health eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairpractice-behavioral-health demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
